title: Airbyte is ignoring `JOB_MAIN_CONTAINER_MEMORY_REQUEST` in .env
body:
### Topic

Can't increase memory of jobs. Ignores all settings made as suggested on [this page](https://docs.airbyte.com/operator-guides/configuring-connector-resources)

EDIT: works at the connection-level, but not at the instance-level or connector-level

### Revelant information

I upgraded from an instance with 8gb of ram to an instance with 32gb of ram, and I just ran into a `Terminating due to java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space` during a sync. I modified the .env file with `JOB_MAIN_CONTAINER_MEMORY_REQUEST=4g` and `JOB_MAIN_CONTAINER_MEMORY_LIMIT=6g` but I'm still seeing this in the sync logs:
```
2023-09-28 02:24:23 INFO i.a.w.p.DockerProcessFactory(create):143 - Creating docker container = destination-redshift-write-39-0-dhrtb with resources io.airbyte.config.ResourceRequirements@2256de7d[cpuRequest=1,cpuLimit=2,memoryRequest=1Gi,memoryLimit=2Gi,additionalProperties={}] and allowedHosts null
```
I've even updated the actor definition with the following sql:
`update actor_definition set resource_requirements = '{"jobSpecific": [{"jobType": "sync", "resourceRequirements": {"memory_limit": "4Gi", "memory_request": "6Gi"}}]}' where name = 'Redshift' and actor_type = 'destination';`

After each step, I've restarted my Airbyte instance and my settings are being ignored.

comments.author: DDynamic
comments.body: I am having the same issue with Airbyte ignoring the instance-level and connector-level overrides outlined [here](https://docs.airbyte.com/operator-guides/configuring-connector-resources/). However, defining a [connection-specific](https://docs.airbyte.com/operator-guides/configuring-connector-resources/) requirement works.

Can you share what you updated the `resource_requirements` with in the `connection` table? I updated everything, but no luck.

EDIT: nvm, got it working. I was trying to use the same value as the **connector** level settings. Setting `{"memory_limit": "4Gi", "memory_request": "6Gi"}` at the **connection** level did it

comments.author: hawkesn
comments.body:
Also observing the same here, modifying the "JOB_MAIN_CONTAINER_MEMORY_REQUEST" set of environment variables are not being respected by the job pods.
Strangely, this is only occurring on `*-read` and `*-write` pods, but the `*-check` pods are fine.

The workaround is by setting the [Configuring Connection-Specific Requirements](https://docs.airbyte.com/operator-guides/configuring-connector-resources#configuring-connection-specific-requirements) - this works for all pods of that Connection

NORMALIZATION_JOB_MAIN_CONTAINER_MEMORY_LIMIT
NORMALIZATION_JOB_MAIN_CONTAINER_MEMORY_REQUEST
```
